label: DSA & Python Coding
description: Write Python, explain your approach, and discuss edge cases and complexity.

questions.prompt: Let's do a coding round. Given integers nums and a target, return the indices of two distinct elements whose sum is target. Return [] if no pair exists. Talk me through your approach, then write Python.
questions.followUp: Why do you check the complement before storing the current number? Walk through [3, 3] with target 6.
questions.idealAnswer: I keep a dictionary from each seen value to its index. Before storing the current value, I check whether its complement has already been seen. This prevents reusing one element and handles duplicates. Return an empty list when there is no solution.

coding.constraints: 0 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100,000. Integers may be negative. Any valid pair is accepted.
coding.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

questions.prompt: Implement a function that checks whether a string of brackets is balanced. Support (), [] and {}. The empty string is valid. Explain why your data structure fits.
questions.followUp: What happens for ([)]? Why is counting opening and closing brackets insufficient?
questions.idealAnswer: Use a stack for unmatched opening brackets. Every closing bracket must match the most recent opener. Reject mismatches and unmatched closers, then require an empty stack at the end.

coding.constraints: Input contains only bracket characters. Length up to 100,000.
coding.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) worst-case space.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the longest substring without repeated characters. Please write a solution that avoids checking every substring.
questions.followUp: In abba, why must the left boundary never move backwards?
questions.idealAnswer: Maintain a sliding window and last-seen indices. On a repeated character, move the left boundary to the maximum of its current value and one past the prior occurrence. Track the largest window length.

coding.constraints: 0 ≤ len(text) ≤ 100,000. Treat Python string characters as individual elements.
coding.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(min(n, alphabet size)) space.

questions.prompt: Merge overlapping closed intervals and return them sorted by start. Touching intervals count as overlapping. Avoid modifying the caller's input.
questions.followUp: How would the condition change if these were half-open intervals?
questions.idealAnswer: Sort a new list by start, then scan while tracking the last merged interval. Extend its end when the next start is within that interval; otherwise append a fresh interval. Copy the interval values to avoid mutating the input.

coding.constraints: Each interval has start ≤ end. Up to 100,000 intervals; input may be unsorted.
coding.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space including sorted input and output.

questions.prompt: Implement binary search on a sorted list. Return any matching index, or -1 when the target is absent. Explain your loop invariant and termination.
questions.followUp: How would you modify this to return the first occurrence of a duplicate target?
questions.idealAnswer: Keep inclusive left and right bounds. If the target exists, it stays inside those bounds. Compare the middle value and discard the impossible half, excluding the middle to guarantee progress. Return -1 when the interval becomes empty.
